teams.name: Atlanta Hawks
teams.history: The franchise began as the Tri-Cities Blackhawks and later played in Milwaukee and St. Louis before moving to Atlanta in 1968. Its NBA title came as the St. Louis Hawks.

teams.name: Boston Celtics
teams.history: One of the NBA original franchises and its most decorated team, with legendary eras led by Bill Russell, Larry Bird and later Paul Pierce.

teams.name: Brooklyn Nets
teams.history: Founded in the ABA as the New Jersey Americans, the franchise later became the New York Nets and played in New Jersey before moving to Brooklyn in 2012. It won two ABA titles, not NBA titles.

teams.name: Charlotte Hornets
teams.history: Charlotte entered the NBA in 1988. The original Hornets relocated in 2002; Charlotte returned as the Bobcats in 2004 and reclaimed the Hornets name in 2014.

teams.name: Chicago Bulls
teams.history: The Bulls became a global sports icon in the 1990s, when Michael Jordan and Scottie Pippen led Chicago to six NBA titles.

teams.name: Cleveland Cavaliers
teams.history: Cleveland joined the league in 1970 and captured its first NBA championship in 2016 behind LeBron James, Kyrie Irving and Kevin Love.

teams.name: Dallas Mavericks
teams.history: The Mavericks joined the NBA in 1980 and won their first championship in 2011 with Dirk Nowitzki leading an upset against Miami.

teams.name: Denver Nuggets
teams.history: Denver began in the ABA as the Denver Rockets, adopted the Nuggets name and joined the NBA in 1976. Nikola Jokic led the club to its first NBA title in 2023.

teams.name: Detroit Pistons
teams.history: The Pistons originated in Fort Wayne before relocating to Detroit in 1957. The Bad Boys won two titles, followed by a defense-led championship in 2004.

teams.name: Golden State Warriors
teams.history: Founded as the Philadelphia Warriors, the club moved to the Bay Area in 1962. A Stephen Curry-led dynasty reshaped the NBA with perimeter shooting.

teams.name: Houston Rockets
teams.history: Founded in San Diego, the Rockets relocated to Houston in 1971. Hakeem Olajuwon led back-to-back championships in 1994 and 1995.

teams.name: Indiana Pacers
teams.history: The Pacers were founded in the ABA and won three ABA championships before joining the NBA in 1976. Those are not counted as NBA titles.

teams.name: LA Clippers
teams.history: Founded as the Buffalo Braves, the team moved to San Diego as the Clippers before relocating to the Los Angeles area in 1984.

teams.name: Los Angeles Lakers
teams.history: The Lakers began in Minneapolis and moved to Los Angeles in 1960. Legends including Magic Johnson, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Kobe Bryant and Shaquille ONeal shaped a championship-rich history.

teams.name: Memphis Grizzlies
teams.history: The Grizzlies joined the NBA in Vancouver in 1995 and moved to Memphis in 2001. The team later became known for its Grit and Grind identity.

teams.name: Miami Heat
teams.history: An NBA expansion team founded in 1988, Miami won its first title with Dwyane Wade and Shaquille ONeal, then added two more during the LeBron James era.

teams.name: Milwaukee Bucks
teams.history: Milwaukee joined the NBA in 1968, won an early title with Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and Oscar Robertson, and another in 2021 led by Giannis Antetokounmpo.

teams.name: Minnesota Timberwolves
teams.history: The Timberwolves joined the NBA in 1989. Kevin Garnett became the franchise defining early superstar, and later generations continued its playoff ambitions.

teams.name: New Orleans Pelicans
teams.history: The franchise began in New Orleans as the Hornets in 2002 following relocation from Charlotte; it adopted the Pelicans name in 2013.

teams.name: New York Knicks
teams.history: A founding NBA franchise playing at Madison Square Garden, New York won titles in the Willis Reed and Walt Frazier era and returned to the summit in 2026.

teams.name: Oklahoma City Thunder
teams.history: The franchise started as the Seattle SuperSonics and moved to Oklahoma City in 2008. Its NBA championships include Seattle in 1979 and Oklahoma City in 2025.

teams.name: Orlando Magic
teams.history: Orlando joined the NBA as a 1989 expansion team and reached NBA Finals behind Shaquille ONeal in 1995 and Dwight Howard in 2009.

teams.name: Philadelphia 76ers
teams.history: The franchise began as the Syracuse Nationals and moved to Philadelphia in 1963. Its title-winning eras included Wilt Chamberlain and Julius Erving.

teams.name: Phoenix Suns
teams.history: Phoenix joined the NBA in 1968 and reached the Finals multiple times, notably in 1976, 1993 and 2021, without winning a championship.

teams.name: Portland Trail Blazers
teams.history: The Trail Blazers entered the NBA in 1970 and won their championship in 1977 behind Bill Walton.

teams.name: Sacramento Kings
teams.history: The franchise traces its history to the Rochester Royals, who won the 1951 NBA championship, before stops in Cincinnati and Kansas City and the move to Sacramento.

teams.name: San Antonio Spurs
teams.history: The Spurs started in the ABA as the Dallas Chaparrals and joined the NBA in 1976. Tim Duncan, Gregg Popovich and a strong team culture produced five NBA titles.

teams.name: Toronto Raptors
teams.history: The Raptors joined the NBA in 1995 as a Canadian expansion team and won their first championship in 2019 led by Kawhi Leonard.

teams.name: Utah Jazz
teams.history: The Jazz were founded in New Orleans in 1974 and relocated to Utah in 1979. John Stockton and Karl Malone led famous Finals runs in the 1990s.

teams.name: Washington Wizards
teams.history: The franchise began as the Chicago Packers and later played as the Baltimore and Washington Bullets, winning the 1978 NBA title before becoming the Wizards.
